list.title: Banking
list.subtitle: Import a bank or credit-card CSV statement, categorize each line (Claude can suggest), then reconcile against the bank's monthly statement.
list.fileTooLarge: File is {{size}} MB; limit is 2 MB.
list.csvHint: Most bank CSV exports work out of the box (Wells Fargo, Chase, BofA, Capital One). The parser auto-detects Date / Description / Amount or Debit+Credit columns.
list.aiUnavailable: AI categorization requires the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret to be set in Cloud Run.

rules.title: Bank rules
rules.subtitle: Auto-categorize bank lines on import. The first matching rule (lowest priority number) wins; AI categorize only runs for lines no rule matched.

placeholders.name: Verizon -> Telephone
placeholders.memoOverride: Leave blank to keep CSV description

rules.empty: No rules yet. Create one above; it will run on every CSV import going forward.

reconcile.title: Reconcile
reconcile.subtitle: Match posted bank transactions against the bank's statement at month-end. When the cleared total equals statement balance minus beginning balance, finalise to lock in the snapshot.
reconcile.reopenConfirm: Reopen this reconciliation? Cleared rows will become editable again.
reconcile.noPostedTransactions: No posted transactions on or before {{date}}.

imports.title: Import from QuickBooks
imports.subtitle: Upload an .iif export to bring over your chart of accounts, customers, vendors, and historical transactions. Transactions post to the ledger as journal entries by default — do NOT also post an opening journal entry, or every balance will be double-counted. To bring over lists only, untick “Import transactions” in the preview and post an opening journal entry instead.
imports.fileTooLarge: File is {{size}} MB. The import accepts up to 12 MB — export from QuickBooks in date-range chunks (File > Utilities > Export) and import each one. Re-importing overlapping ranges is safe for unchanged transactions: already-posted transactions are skipped as duplicates. (A transaction edited in QuickBooks since an earlier import posts again — the import warns when it detects that.)
imports.dropHint: Drop a .iif file or click below to choose one.

missing.title: Missing accounts referenced by transactions
missing.hint: These account names appear in the file's transactions but aren't in your chart of accounts and aren't being created from this file's account section. We've guessed a type/subtype from each name — review and edit, then confirm. Auto-created accounts are committed before transactions post, so the JEs land cleanly.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.hint: Each posting transaction becomes one journal_entry. Sign rule: positive amount = debit, negative = credit. Transactions whose accounts aren't in the chart of accounts after the lists step are skipped and reported.

done.title: Import complete.
done.paymentsLinked: , {{n}} linked to vendor/customer payment records (1099s, statements)
done.paymentsBackfilled: , {{n}} payment record(s) backfilled for previously imported transactions

excluded.title_one: {{count}} transaction block from the file was NOT imported (data errors found before posting):
excluded.title_other: {{count}} transaction blocks from the file were NOT imported (data errors found before posting):
excluded.hint: Fix these rows in the file and re-import it — already-posted transactions are skipped as duplicates (as long as they weren't edited in QuickBooks since the last import; an edited transaction posts again as a new entry).

unlinked.title_one: {{count}} payee posted to the ledger only — no vendor/customer payment record was written:
unlinked.title_other: {{count}} payees posted to the ledger only — no vendor/customer payment record was written:
unlinked.hint: These names didn't match any vendor or customer (check spelling/punctuation, QuickBooks “Other Names”, or employees). Their amounts won't appear in 1099 totals, payroll registers, or statements until matching payment records exist. To fix: create the missing vendor/customer (or correct its spelling) and re-import this file — the transactions are skipped as duplicates and their payment records are backfilled automatically.

mileage.title: Mileage
mileage.subtitle: Log business trips with the IRS standard mileage rate, then batch-post a date range to a journal entry (DR Vehicle/Mileage Expense, CR Owner Reimbursement). The rate at log time is locked on the trip — IRS rate changes won't silently shift past deductions.
mileage.postEnabledTitle: Post a date range to a JE

empty.title: No trips logged yet
empty.description: Log your first business trip — the form pre-fills with the current IRS standard mileage rate. Posting batches all logged trips in a date range into one journal entry.

preview.label: Deduction:
preview.empty: Fill in miles + rate to preview the deduction.

post.title: Post mileage to GL
post.hint: Sums every logged trip in the date range and writes ONE journal entry: DR {{debit}}, CR {{credit}}. Each posted trip gets stamped with the JE id and locked from edits.
